beats.narration_text: Bonjour, this is Liam, in for Bear. There is a skill called sri-explainer that most fellows will read as another Brutalist explainer. It is not. It takes one chapter of a Prof Sridhar book and turns it into a video that teaches what that chapter is about — in Sridhar's own written voice. So I asked Claude to read the whole SKILL dot m-d and tell me what makes it its own thing.

beats.role_note: The chapter → beat spine. This is the SKILL's own default act structure — HOOK → SETUP → MECHANISM → GROUNDING → (DYNAMICS) → VERDICT → YOUR TURN → OUTRO.
beats.narration_text: Here is the spine, fixed — because it mirrors the chapter's own order. Cold open. Then HOOK — the chapter's own opening scene, a real image when the chapter has one. Then SETUP — the potential or the problem, equation on screen. Then MECHANISM — the two to four turns where something is actually decided. Then GROUNDING — the chapter's own numeric example, on screen. Optionally DYNAMICS. Then the verdict, the your turn, and the outro. This order is not this skill's invention. It is the chapter's.

props.heading: The chapter is the storyboard.
props.body: HOOK → SETUP → MECHANISM → GROUNDING → optional DYNAMICS → VERDICT → YOUR TURN → OUTRO. The chapter’s own section order becomes the video’s own act order. Do not reinvent an arc; adapt the chapter’s.
props.quote: The chapter’s own section order — hook → setup → derivation → grounding → (dynamics, if present) → bridge-forward — is the video’s own act order.

beats.role_note: Mechanism 2 — the Sridhar register: NEGATION-BEFORE-AFFIRMATION; short punch sentences; concrete physical-scale anchors.
beats.narration_text: Second decision. The Sridhar register — derived directly from reading quantum dash mechanics dash vol one, not invented. The move you hear most in the book is negation before affirmation. State what a result is NOT before affirming what it IS. Short punch sentences after a longer explanatory one. Concrete physical scale over abstract claim. A number always anchored to something felt — an e V, a room temperature k B T — never a bare symbol.

props.heading: Negate before affirm.
props.body: Three moves the book uses over and over: (1) negation-before-affirmation — say what a result is NOT before you say what it IS; (2) short punch-sentence after a longer explanatory one; (3) every number anchored to something felt (an eV, a room-temperature k_B·T) — never a bare symbol.
props.quote: State what a result is NOT before affirming what it IS; short punch-sentences after a longer explanatory one; concrete physical-scale comparisons over abstract claims; numbers always anchored to something felt (an eV, a room-temperature k_B T), never a bare symbol.

beats.role_note: Mechanism 3 — DERIVATION-COMPRESSION LAW. Never all N steps. Extract 2–4 decision points; one beat each.
beats.narration_text: Third decision, and it is a compression rule. Never narrate every algebra line of a derivation — that is lecture capture, not an explainer. Extract the two to four points where something is actually decided — the moment a continuous quantity collapses to a discrete one, the moment a boundary condition kills a term — and give each its own illustrated beat. One beat per genuine turn, never one beat per algebra step.

verdict pill 'COMPRESS · never per algebra step' lands

props.heading: One beat per turn.
props.body: A decision point is where something COLLAPSES — a continuous quantity becomes discrete, a boundary condition kills a term, an approximation is finally justified. Pick 2-4 of those from the chapter's derivation; give each its own illustrated beat. Everything else in that derivation is preparation and stays off the mic.
props.quote: Never narrate all N steps of the chapter's derivation verbatim — that is lecture-capture, not an explainer. Extract the 2–4 points where something is actually decided … and give each its own illustrated beat.
props.cite: sri-explainer SKILL.md · Hard rules · DERIVATION-COMPRESSION LAW

beats.role_note: Mechanism 4 — GOLDEN-TEST-ON-SCREEN LAW. Any number shown carries its own check (ratio, limit, conservation), spoken and shown. Sharper than parent DOUBLE-CHECK LAW.
beats.narration_text: Fourth decision, and this is the honesty gate. Any number shown on screen carries its own check. The ratio it satisfies, the limit it reduces to, the conservation law it obeys — spoken and shown. This is sharper than the parent's generic double check law because the book's own system prompt makes it non negotiable. Never assert a numeric result is physically correct without an independent checkable comparison on screen.

props.heading: Every number checks itself.
props.body: A number lands on screen with the check that validates it — the ratio to a known quantity, the limit it reduces to, the conservation law it obeys. The check is spoken AND shown. This is the parent chassis's DOUBLE-CHECK LAW sharpened for physics: no un-checked numeric result, ever.
props.quote: Any number shown carries its own check, spoken and shown (the ratio/limit it satisfies) — sharper than the parent's generic DOUBLE-CHECK LAW because the book's own system prompt makes this non-negotiable: never assert a numeric result is physically correct without an independent, checkable comparison on screen.
props.cite: sri-explainer SKILL.md · Hard rules · GOLDEN-TEST-ON-SCREEN LAW

beats.role_note: Mechanism 5 — HANDOFF-FROM-THE-CHAPTER LAW + BRIDGE-HONESTY LAW. YOUR TURN drawn from chapter's LLM Exercises; VERDICT names what the chapter didn't resolve.
beats.narration_text: Fifth decision, and it is about where the YOUR TURN prompt comes from. It comes from the chapter itself — from the L L M exercises section, if the chapter has one. Adapt, do not invent fresh. Same instinct as skill teardown's self demo law — the source's own material is the demo. Then the verdict states plainly what the chapter did NOT resolve and which future chapter does — matching the book's own what comes next honesty.

props.heading: The handoff is the chapter's.
props.body: YOUR TURN adapts a prompt from the chapter's own 'LLM Exercises' section (adapt, don't invent). VERDICT states plainly what the chapter did NOT resolve and which future chapter does — matching the book's own 'What Comes Next' honesty. Never imply the chapter closed a question it left open.
props.quote: The Your Turn prompt is always drawn from the chapter's own "LLM Exercises" section (adapt, don't invent fresh) — the same instinct as skill-teardown's SELF-DEMO LAW: use the source's own material as the demo.
props.cite: sri-explainer SKILL.md · Hard rules · HANDOFF-FROM-THE-CHAPTER LAW

beats.role_note: FALSIFIABILITY / documented limitation. What sri-explainer needs that this reel does NOT execute (a chapter file, claude-sri wired in, factcheck on chapter numbers).
beats.narration_text: Now the limitation of this film. Actually running sri dash explainer end to end needs three things this Brutalist toolkit does not ship today. A chapter file from a Prof Sridhar book. The claude dash sri channel added to brand underscore variant dot py and to the allowed voices list in generate underscore audio underscore kokoro dot py. And a real end to end review pass on that chapter's own numbers. What you have watched is the skill's mechanism read from its own SKILL dot m-d — quotes verbatim, cites shown. When you run it yourself on a real Sridhar chapter, this is the doctrine your Claude is following.

props.heading: The honest limitation.
props.body: A real sri-explainer build needs three things this reel does not execute: (1) a chapter file from a Prof Sridhar book; (2) the claude-sri channel added to generate_audio_kokoro.py's ALLOWED_VOICES and brand_variant.py's channel table; (3) a factcheck pass on that chapter's own numbers. What you watched is the skill's mechanism read from its own SKILL.md — quotes verbatim, cites shown. When you run it on a real chapter, this is the doctrine your Claude is following.

beats.role_note: VERDICT artifact — six lines recapping the split. Bookends inherited; chassis inherited; register owned; handoff from chapter; when to reach for it and when to reach elsewhere.
beats.narration_text: So the split. Bookends inherited. Chassis inherited from deep dash explainer or ai dash explainer, chapter dependent. Register owned — Sridhar, in his own voice, negation before affirmation, every number checked. Handoff drawn from the chapter itself. Reach for it when your source is a Prof Sridhar chapter and you want the video written the way he writes.

artifactLines: Bookends INHERITED — cold open, hesitant writer, verdict, YOUR TURN, title outro from ai-explainer.
Chassis INHERITED — deep-explainer for a multi-section chapter, ai-explainer for a single-mechanism chapter.
Register OWNED — Sridhar, first person, negate-before-affirm, every number anchored, every check on screen.
Spine follows the chapter's own order — HOOK → SETUP → MECHANISM → GROUNDING → (DYNAMICS) → VERDICT.
Handoff drawn from the chapter's own LLM Exercises; verdict names what the chapter left open.
REACH FOR IT when your source is a Prof Sridhar chapter. REACH ELSEWHERE — ai-explainer for a concept; cli-explainer for a build.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude Code. Read the skill file. Then pick one chapter of a Prof Sridhar book — or any textbook you know deeply — and ask Claude to plan a sri dash explainer of it. Do not author beats yet. First surface the chapter's own act map — hook, setup, mechanism, grounding, dynamics if present — and pick the two to four derivation turns worth a beat each. If your source is not a chapter, ask Claude to tell you which sibling — ai dash explainer, deep dash explainer, cli dash explainer — is the right skill instead.
